verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Iran Unresolved; GOOGL Hits Stop; JOLTS Binary at 10 AM
verdict.rationale_short: Iran talks remain suspended and Brent sits at $94.58 — just $2.42 from the $97 mandatory XLE cover trigger. The 30Y closed again near 5.01% on June 1, making this the third consecutive session without a clean sub-5.0% close; the Day-2 confirmation sequence required to unlock the NVDA add zone and high-conviction BUY upgrade is fully reset. GOOGL fell to $376.42 intraday on June 2, breaching the $378 daily-close invalidation established in the night brief. META is down approximately 4-5% and AAPL is down 1.86%, narrowing the market's leadership to NVDA and MSFT exclusively. JOLTS (April) releases at 10:00 AM ET — a reading above 8M raises Warsh June 17 hike probability and deepens the STEP ASIDE case; below 7M would be equity-friendly but insufficient to upgrade the framework absent Iran and 30Y resolution.

bear_case: The S&P 500's six-session winning streak from mid-May through June 1 was built on two pillars — Iran MoU optimism and NVDA COMPUTEX momentum — and the first pillar has now collapsed without the index fully acknowledging it. Iran talks are suspended, Brent is $2.42 from a level that would force the XLE short cover and confirm a supply shock, and the 30Y has failed to close below 5.00% for three consecutive sessions. With GOOGL breaking its stop, META down 4-5%, and AAPL selling off at index records, the equal-weight tape diverges sharply from the headline. JOLTS at 10:00 AM ET is the near-term binary: a reading above 8M combined with Friday's NFP (consensus ~100K) printing above 150K would make Warsh's June 17 FOMC a live hike event, collapsing the 30Y sub-5.0% narrative entirely and requiring an exit of all long positions simultaneously. Invalidation of the STEP ASIDE: if Iran talks formally resume AND the 30Y closes below 5.00% for two consecutive sessions, the framework returns to HOLD.
